evals.prompt: Look over my branch before I push. Heads up that main is already red on the flaky auth test, so don't wait for green. I added a formatDuration helper in src/lib/time.ts.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report in the Local review format: the new helper flagged against the live duration formatter already exported next door, the failing auth test shown as baseline, and an unchanged working tree.
assertions: Edits no file
Does not require a green suite to begin; the auth failure appears in the Baseline line, not as a finding
Locates the existing exported formatter and cites its path and a live call site in a Context: line
States the range reviewed as a ref pair or merge-base range
Every finding carries file:line, a Why: line, and a Fix: line that could be committed as written

evals.prompt: Review this diff, it removes the retry wrapper around the sync write in src/workers/sync.ts since the write is idempotent now. Don't change anything, just tell me if it's safe.
evals.expected_output: A report that traces the writers of the delayed state outside the diff, finds the scheduler that can still produce it, and reports the removal as a regression with the trigger named.
assertions: Reads outside the diff to find every writer of the state the retry handled
Names the trigger and the consequence for the removed guard
Does not accept fewer lines as proof of safety
Reads references/context-errors.md before applying its rubric, and lists only reference files actually read in this session under Reference evidence
Each reference listed under Reference evidence carries a short quoted excerpt
Edits no file

evals.prompt: Tidy this up. Two of the route handlers I touched each normalize the Stripe response by hand, and I'm pretty sure there's a mapper for that somewhere in src/payments.
evals.expected_output: Both handlers rewritten onto the shared mapper after confirming it has live callers and matching semantics, the affected tests run with the result quoted, and a summary of what changed and what was left.
assertions: Confirms the shared mapper has live callers and handles the boundary cases the hand-rolled code handled before switching to it
Applies the change rather than only reporting it
Runs the tests the change affects after the edit and reports their actual result
Quotes the last line of the check output rather than paraphrasing it
Summary lists what was applied, what was left and why, and the check results
Does not commit, push, or open a PR

evals.prompt: Simplify this diff. There's a guard in src/cache/read.ts for an empty snapshot that I think is dead now. Careful, I have unrelated uncommitted edits in that same file I still need.
evals.expected_output: The guard kept because a background worker outside the diff still writes the empty snapshot, the uncertainty reported with the writer named, and the user's other edits in the file untouched.
assertions: Inspects the writers of the snapshot state, including the background worker outside the diff
Does not delete the guard while a writer of the reachable state exists; reports the writer and the uncertainty instead
Does not run git restore or otherwise roll back the whole file; the user's unrelated edits survive
Applies any other supported simplification in the diff rather than stopping at the guard

evals.prompt: deslop this branch, the agent left comments everywhere and there's a bunch of `as any`
evals.expected_output: Findings grouped by slop category with file:line, comments and casts fixed at the source without changing runtime behavior, and stale comments quoted alongside the line that refutes them.
assertions: Reads references/ai-slop-patterns.md and references/severity-rubric.md and lists them under Reference evidence with excerpts
Groups findings by category, not by file
Fixes `as any` at the type's source or with a type guard rather than a different cast
Flags only patterns inside the diff; pre-existing comments outside touched functions are not findings
Attempts the type check after the edits and reports its actual outcome, including a command that could not run

evals.prompt: Audit these tests in my PR before I merge. I added a test in src/lib/slug.spec.ts that mocks the entire slugify module and asserts the mock returned what I told it to return.
evals.expected_output: The mock-only test flagged under the test gate as a confirmed finding, since it asserts the mock's own return value rather than real slugify output, with a fix that asserts on the real function's output instead; the rest of the diff reviewed normally, and references/test-gate.md read only because the diff touched a test file.
assertions: Reads references/test-gate.md because the diff adds or changes a test, and lists it under Reference evidence
Flags the mock-only test as confirmed, naming the mocked module and the self-referential assertion
Fix asserts on the real slugify output rather than the mock's return value
Does not treat this as a suite-wide prune; no coverage target or campaign language appears
Files the finding in the same confirmed/plausible tiers as the rest of the report, not a separate section

evals.prompt: Can you review my branch before I push? It's a harmless cleanup of createReservation in src/reservations/create.ts, the route already does those checks.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report that flags the removed party-size validation as a regression because the waitlist CSV import calls createReservation without the route's checks, names the corrupted seat count a bad row produces, and clears the removed unknown-slot check as dead code.
assertions: Reports the removed party-size check in src/reservations/create.ts as a regression
Names the waitlist CSV import as a caller that reaches createReservation without the route's validation
States a concrete wrong outcome for a bad party size, such as a NaN or negative seat count that lets a slot overbook
Does not report the removed unknown-slot check as a regression
Edits no file

evals.prompt: Review my branch please. I changed findProduct in src/catalog/lookup.ts to throw instead of returning null and updated the product route to match.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report that greps the callers of findProduct, finds the reorder planner still relying on a null return, and reports that one unknown SKU now aborts the nightly reorder instead of being skipped.
assertions: Identifies src/orders/reorder.ts as a caller of findProduct that the diff did not update
States that an unknown SKU now throws out of the reorder run where it used to be skipped
Proposes a fix that restores skipping unknown SKUs in the reorder planner
Does not report the updated product route as broken
States the range reviewed as a ref pair or merge-base range

evals.prompt: Review this before I open a PR. Expense submissions kept failing whenever receipt storage had a blip, so saveReceipt in src/receipts/save.ts handles the error itself now.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report that flags the new catch as a discarded error: saveReceipt returns a receipt key after a failed upload, so submitExpense records the key and discards the only copy of the file, with a fix that lets the caller see the failure.
assertions: Flags the new catch in src/receipts/save.ts as swallowing the storage failure while still returning a receipt key
Names src/expenses/submit.ts as the caller that treats the failed upload as a success
States that the temporary upload is discarded even though the receipt was never stored
Proposes a fix that lets the caller tell a failed upload from a stored one
Edits no file

evals.prompt: tidy this branch before I push, I added signature verification for the carrier webhooks in src/webhooks/verify.ts
evals.expected_output: The hand-rolled hex encoder and constant-time comparison replaced with node:crypto built-ins while a wrong-length signature still returns false, the webhook tests run with their result reported, and nothing committed.
assertions: Replaces the hand-rolled comparison with timingSafeEqual from node:crypto
Replaces the hand-rolled hex encoder with the built-in hex output of the digest or Buffer
States that a signature of the wrong length is still rejected rather than throwing
Runs the webhook tests after the edit and reports their actual result
Does not commit, push, or open a PR

evals.prompt: Tidy this up for me. The branch adds scheduled ticket exports by email and a JSON option on the existing download.
evals.expected_output: The delivery registry and strategy interface removed so the scheduled export calls the mailer directly, because email is its only strategy and call site; the formatter lookup kept because the download and the scheduled export both use it; tests run and nothing committed.
assertions: Removes or inlines the delivery strategy registry from src/export/delivery.ts
Cites email being the only registered strategy or the single call site as the reason for removing the registry
Leaves the formatter lookup in src/export/formatters.ts in place
Runs the export tests after the edit and reports their actual result
Does not commit, push, or open a PR

evals.prompt: Review my changes on this branch before I push. It adds a preview page so people can see where a short link goes.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report with no findings: the link target interpolated into the preview markup is escaped by the html template tag and limited to http and https at creation, both outside the diff, so the branch is ready to push.
assertions: States plainly that the branch is ready to push
Does not report the link target interpolated in src/http/handlers/preview.ts as an injection or escaping defect
Lists no finding that asks for a code change
Edits no file
States the range reviewed as a ref pair or merge-base range
